fact_reason: 'You put down a deposit on an apartment, that money's gone, it covers holding the place.' A rental security deposit belongs to the tenant and must be returned at move-out minus unpaid rent or damage beyond normal wear and tear (state tenant guides, e.g. ohiolegalhelp.org, CA Attorney General).

'Alexia had already put her hands on the wheel at ten and two, exactly as the booklet showed.' Current NHTSA guidance (see coastlineacademy.com/article/drivers-ed-steering-wheel-hand-position-9-and-3-not-10-and-2) is 9 and 3, because 10 and 2 puts hands and arms in the airbag's path.
age_reason: Fits grade 12; probability versus promise is handled lightly, and 'indemnify' is used correctly.

fact_reason: 'She sat in the driver's seat of the borrowed Corolla with her hands at ten and two, the way the pamphlet showed.' Current NHTSA guidance (see coastlineacademy.com/article/drivers-ed-steering-wheel-hand-position-9-and-3-not-10-and-2) is 9 and 3, because 10 and 2 puts hands and arms in the airbag's path.
age_reason: Fits grade 12; the metaphor about holding on and giving room is earned; 'drafting a subpoena for a collision' is forced.

fact_reason: 'the red of the lower half and the blood at the corners of her mouth' / 'the corset is grey because her actual corset was grey'. In The Broken Column her lower body is wrapped in a white sheet, the corset straps are white, and there is no blood at her mouth, only tears (NYU Medical Humanities, medhum.med.nyu.edu/view/12902).
age_reason: Art critique that argues with its own method; vocabulary and ambiguity fit grade 12.

fact_reason: 'She ran the letters again from the beginning. Serine, histidine, glycine, leucine.' Read from the first letter, UCC AUG GGA CUU decodes as serine, methionine, glycine, leucine; there is no CAU (histidine) or GGG codon in that frame.
age_reason: Grade 12 prose, but the thinking is mostly a decoding puzzle and 'a smirk ... frankly intransigent' is a slightly forced word.
Plot slip and thin ideas for grade 12: 'Their sister's moods were mercurial... but Danny had always thought Chloe's were worse' confuses who is who, and the thinking stays at concrete bead-threading.

Plot loses track: a freshly cut cereal-box strip bears the grandfather's scorecard and 'placement exam, failed, retake granted', and 'six months of knowing the answer' contradicts the days-long timeline.

fact_reason: 'chase ninety more cents an hour' / 'quitting over ninety cents'. Theo earns 'nine dollars and change' against Alex's $7.25, a gap of at least $1.75 an hour, not ninety cents.
age_reason: Money versus attachment is a fitting value conflict; the 'ninety more cents' figure does not match the wage numbers.

fact_reason: 'Black, wings folded, hanging dead from the thorn necklace', 'crowded with monkey faces', plus a butterfly at lower left and 'a single fuchsia ribbon' on her forehead. In the painting the hummingbird's wings are outstretched, there is one monkey, and the butterflies are clips in her hair; there is no forehead ribbon (Wikipedia, Self-Portrait with Thorn Necklace and Hummingbird).

Devon 'sketched the parabola opening upward, then the line slicing through it' and it is 'the same picture' in which 'the parabola rode above the line' between the crossings; also 'the line rode above a downward-opening parabola' between crossings. Between two intersection points a line lies above an upward-opening parabola and below a downward-opening one, so both setups are geometrically impossible.

'Her first attempt gave her a field of almost a trillion volts per metre... she had multiplied by the constant instead of dividing.' Multiplying the charge density by 8.85e-12 gives a far smaller number than dividing, not a larger one; the described error could not produce a trillion V/m.

'a single person deciding, on a Thursday in March, to walk through a particular door and press a particular button.' 28 March 1979 was a Wednesday, and Commons divisions are counted by MPs walking through lobbies, not by pressing buttons.
age_reason: Institutional tradeoffs and an unresolved question about trust suit grade 12.

fact_reason: uncertain: 'From the fat one near his thumb up to the thin one nearest his face.' I believe the G string, not the E, is the one nearer the player's chin, but a web search summary said the opposite, so I could not confirm it.

The $250 million purchase 'had cost ... less than a third of what her school district had spent on a football stadium.' That implies a stadium over $750 million; the most expensive US high-school stadiums cost roughly $70-175 million (NBC DFW / ASU Magazine reports on Katy's $70M Legacy Stadium).

Her grandmother was 'fired from a print shop for union organizing'. The story endorses the mother correcting the uncle, who calls this illegal. Under the National Labor Relations Act it is illegal for a private employer to fire an employee for union organizing (NLRB, Section 8(a)).
age_reason: State action versus private power, with an 'accurate and antiquated' ambivalence that suits the band.

fact_reason: 'got one that said GGU, arginine. She walked the ribbon until she found GCC.' GGU codes glycine, GCC codes alanine, and GGU does not pair with GCC; the AUG card also 'matches' the AUG codon identically, whereas an anticodon is complementary (UAC). Also 'They're turgid' describes wilted, soft seedlings; turgid means swollen and firm.
age_reason: Fits grade 12; 'They're turgid' is used for wilting seedlings, the opposite of its meaning.

fact_reason: 'his two hundred and ten dollars, left alone, would quietly become more.' The money is in his sock drawer; cash kept at home earns no interest and does not grow, only money in an interest-bearing account does.
age_reason: Appropriate interest/credit dilemma; 'putative door' and 'determinism' feel forced.

fact_reason: At ten past two Priya is still 'trimming the foot of a cup with a loop tool' (leather-hard clay), and the cups go into the 4:00 firing that day and come out 'glossy'. Greenware must be bone-dry before firing, or the steam cracks or bursts it; freshly trimmed cups cannot be fired two hours later.
age_reason: Strong grade-12 values conflict; the kiln timeline in the ending is slightly confusing.

fact_reason: 'He moved from Tennessee.' / 'So he doesn't pay ... Same building, same contract' / 'Now you've got it.' Right-to-work status depends on the state where the work is done, not on where the worker came from, so Danny is under the same dues rules as Charles (Cornell LII 'right to work state'; state-law-applies-where-work-is-performed rule).

'Even, the review implied, when the positive ones outnumbered them five to one.' The 2001 Baumeister review (citing Gottman) says good interactions must outnumber bad ones by at least five to one for the good to prevail, not that bad still wins at five to one (checked in the review's text).
age_reason: Wry feedback story with an unresolved why; the typo 'repotating' is minor.
Misused word ('the usual Saturday vernacular of the shop: half-finished lattes') and a tangled Saturday/Sunday shift plot, with the concept explained by a character rather than explored.
Tangled plot: a POV jump to the counselor reveals 'the withdrawal from the private college... logged in August' for a student still in class, a subplot that is never resolved.
The narrative loses track of its protagonist's name ('Eella' four times against 'Ella'), 'debilitate her whole plan' is a misuse, and the closing 'Doors close at noon... We'll make it' is confusing.
Ending loses track of events: Dana 'did the aquifer thing yesterday', then 'No, mine was the football match... I did the film festival instead.'

fact_reason: 'He asked the youngest the four questions as tradition required.' By tradition the youngest child asks the Four Questions (Wikipedia, Four Questions). Also 'sundown was around 7:40, which gave him two hours and forty minutes in the small room before the Bernsteins needed the lobby' is wrong arithmetic: 5:00 to the 8:00 booking is three hours; 2h40 is only the time until sundown.
age_reason: Competing pulls of fidelity and adaptation, nuanced transitions; well matched.

fact_reason: 'He swapped the two values, ran the test again, and watched the bar turn green.' Swapping assertEquals arguments only changes the failure message; it cannot turn a failing equality check into a passing one. The fact itself is stated correctly.

Priya's mom, endorsed: the missing 13 percent includes students who 'graduated somewhere else, some moved.' The adjusted cohort graduation rate removes students who transfer out, and a transfer who graduates counts as a graduate; the 13 percent are students who did not graduate within four years (source: NCES ACGR definition).
age_reason: Mature graduation reflection on missing classmates; fits grade 12.

fact_reason: 'Thirty-eight, again ... thirty-eight was what his own arithmetic kept insisting' while he counted the citric acid cycle only once. Counting one turn per glucose loses the second turn's ATP, 3 NADH and FADH2 (about 12 ATP in the 38 accounting), so the one-turn total cannot come out at 36 or 38; the story's worked count is wrong.
age_reason: Plot contradicts its own central problem: 'Maxime kept getting thirty-six' then 'Thirty-eight, again... thirty-eight was what his own arithmetic kept insisting.'

fact_reason: 'I pulled my main tuning slide out a bit the way he had shown me, which raises the pitch.' Pulling a trumpet's tuning slide out lengthens the tubing and lowers the pitch; a flat player pushes it in (source: trumpet tuning guides, e.g. tomplay.com trumpet tuner).
age_reason: Rich abstract question about standards, but inconsistent schedule ('Tuesday nights' vs 'Thursday beginners' band').

fact_reason: 'Claudia wished her sister a happy birthday, promised a cheerful day, and asked her to come.' Tablet 291 invites Lepidina to Claudia Severa's own birthday on 11 September ('for the day of the celebration of my birthday'). Claudia does not wish Lepidina a happy birthday (Wikipedia, Vindolanda tablets; romaninscriptionsofbritain.org Tab.Vindol. 291).
age_reason: Historiographical disagreement dramatized with genuine ambiguity at the right level.

fact_reason: A state senator explains that his statewide crossing-safety bill failed with 55 supporters because US Senate cloture needs 60 of 100 votes. A state bill is not voted on in the US Senate, and the 60-vote cloture rule is a US Senate rule, not a rule of state legislatures in general.
age_reason: Civic process with a real tension between majority rule and supermajority; the procedural exposition is somewhat heavy.

fact_reason: A 17-year-old signs the climbing-gym liability waiver herself and is let climb, framed as valid informed agreement (the story even lists 'sign when you're eighteen' as the alternative). A minor's signature on a waiver is voidable and gyms require a parent or guardian to sign for under-18s (nonprofitrisk.org; standard climbing-gym minor waivers).

age_reason: Garbled prose confuses the scene: 'involuntary andavenous for completeness' and 'forty-some people in caps and gowns pushed caps and gowns were actually in the kitchen, clogging a chair'.

fact_reason: 'Othello says it, right at the end, when he's giving up everything.' The 'pride, pomp, and circumstance' line comes in Othello's farewell to his profession in Act 3, Scene 3, not at the end of the play (Wikipedia, 'Pomp and Circumstance Marches'). The injected fact itself is stated correctly.

'Keira drew petitioner, the student's side' and the unanswered 'Schools aren't Congress. So how does it even apply?' In the real banner case (Morse v. Frederick) the school principal was the petitioner, and the First Amendment has applied to public-school students since Tinker (1969), so the story wrongly treats that as an open question (Wikipedia, Morse v. Frederick; Tinker v. Des Moines).

'monthly carbon dioxide measurements from a station on a volcano in Hawaii called Mauna Loa, marching across a century.' The Mauna Loa record only began in March 1958, so it spans under 70 years, not a century (Wikipedia, Keeling Curve).

'She wrote the signs in like weather reports, plus, plus, minus' The derivative is positive below 4, negative between 4 and 11 and positive above 11, so the sign chart is plus, minus, plus, which the story itself gives later.

The story presents cooking the week's chicken and rice on the weekend and eating it from the fridge through 'Friday's dinner' as a working plan. USDA says cooked leftovers keep 3-4 days in the refrigerator (usda.gov leftovers guidance). Anything for later in the week should be frozen.
age_reason: Thinking reads well below grade 12: the central insight is learning to read a shelf tag ('Unit price... Cost per gram'), with only a brief closing nod to anything abstract.

fact_reason: 'That is all transcription and translation are': the tRNA anticodon-to-codon matching he describes is translation only; transcription is the separate step of copying DNA into mRNA. The story endorses his summary ('He knew what he knew'). The tRNA fact itself is stated correctly.

age_reason: The plot loses count of its seniors: 'the five of them up there, the seniors' and 'The five seniors drank', then 'It's only adjourning for you two' / 'Three'; Dana is also said to be 'coming back'.

fact_reason: 'Not by much, a dollar and change on five hundred.' $500 at 3% compounded monthly for one year is $515.21 against $515.00 annually, a difference of about 21 cents.
age_reason: Fits grade 12; the longhand compounding calculation is concrete and the decision is plausible.

fact_reason: 'watching twelve twelve-year-olds... Coach Reyes, who had handed her the mites' Mites are the 8-and-under division in USA Hockey; twelve-year-olds play Peewee (Wikipedia, Minor ice hockey).

'Two giant detectors, same tunnel, same collisions.' ATLAS and CMS sit at different collision points on the LHC ring and record different collisions, which is part of why their results were independent (source: home.cern, Large Hadron Collider page).
age_reason: Replication theme tied to a self-deceiving memory; fits grade 12.

fact_reason: 'She began to drift left... Madison looked over her right shoulder.' When moving left to merge, the driver must check the blind spot over the left shoulder, not the right.
age_reason: Driver's-ed insight is practical but reflection lifts it to the band.

fact_reason: The story has Passover listed on Friday the fifteenth and a Seder on Thursday evening. The Jewish calendar never puts the first day of Passover on a Monday, Wednesday or Friday (the 'lo BaDU Pesach' rule; jhom.com, Chabad), so a Thursday-evening first Seder cannot happen.
age_reason: Strong grade 12 fit, with small slips (the typo 'great-aut', and some hall/dining-room timeline confusion).

fact_reason: 'standing under the bare loquat tree' in the cold. The loquat (Eriobotrya japonica) is evergreen, so it does not stand bare in winter (UF/IFAS ST235; Wikipedia 'Loquat').

'Eleven hours,' she said. 'She's counting today as three. One left after this.' 11 - 3 = 8, not 1. Priya said earlier that she had twelve hours left, so three hours today cannot bring her to the 'forty of forty' Mara then stamps.
age_reason: Teleology woven naturally into a choice about motive; hour-count arithmetic is a little muddled.

fact_reason: 'The problem arrived at measure 194. Her recapitulation bracket closed there... Twelve more measures' In Mozart's K. 332 first movement the recapitulation starts at m. 133 and restates the whole 93-bar exposition in the tonic (Wikipedia, Piano Sonata No. 12), so it cannot end at m. 194 with a 12-bar coda to follow.
age_reason: Fits grade 12, but some required words are misused, e.g. 'politely unperfumed by her silence', 'the mirror that stigmatized nothing'.

fact_reason: 'between "vermilion" and "vernal," sat her grandfather's word, which turned out to be "vertigo."' Alphabetically, vertigo comes after vernal, not between vermilion and vernal. Also, six halvings of a roughly 1,000-page dictionary leave about 16 pages, not 'a single page'.

'her uncle, who installed them [wind turbines], call the job a sinecure compared with the refinery work... safe and indoor and dull.' Installing wind turbines is outdoor work at height, not a safe indoor job; the story presents this uncorrected.
age_reason: Rich competing values suit grade 12; 'a place that had acclimated' is a slightly strained use.

fact_reason: 'Justin played the open A, the tuner's needle settling dead center... It read 440' (on a cello). A cello's open A string is A3 = 220 Hz, not 440 Hz (Wikipedia, Cello: open strings C2, G2, D3, A3); the octave fact itself is stated correctly.

age_reason: Reads middle-school: plain short exchanges ('Fine. RNA polymerase.' 'She tried.') and a library-copy analogy with no abstract principle or competing values for grade 12.

fact_reason: 'blocked on the thrust stage in the main house, with the audience in a single dark wedge facing the action' / 'composing for a single viewpoint'. A thrust stage has the audience on three sides (Wikipedia, Thrust stage); a single facing audience describes a proscenium stage.
age_reason: Varied, nuanced prose and an open fairness-versus-quality question fit grade 12 well.

fact_reason: 'Glucose and oxygen become carbon dioxide and water. Six of each, in, six of each, out, plus the energy.' One glucose and six O2 go in (C6H12O6 + 6 O2 -> 6 CO2 + 6 H2O), not six of each; the story's closing explanation gets the stoichiometry wrong.
age_reason: Band-fit reflection, but the respiration equation is restated several times in a textbook way.

fact_reason: 'So the list was broken before, with the four names, and broken after, with none.' 'Right.' The same NOT IN query on the same data with the NULL present cannot return four names on Tuesday and zero rows later; with a NULL in the list NOT IN always returns nothing, so the NULL could not have caused the four wrong names. The injected fact itself is stated correctly.
age_reason: Plot contradicts itself: the NULL first yields 'four names', then the rerun 'with the blank still in place' yields 'nothing at all', which leaves the mechanism muddled; 'suture' is also forced.

fact_reason: 'Both of them have derivative six x minus twelve. Maximum at x equals two.' f(x)=3x^2-12x opens upward, so x=2 is a minimum, not a maximum (the 'peaks' in Kyle's sketch are troughs). The injected fact itself is stated correctly.
age_reason: Fits; the 'speciation' aside is forced.

fact_reason: 'Maybe Saturday. With a balloon.' / 'With the loud one.' The story ends with a teen agreeing to ignite a hydrogen balloon at home for her nine-year-old sister; hydrogen balloon ignition is a hazardous demonstration for trained teachers, not a home activity.
age_reason: Fits the band; 'metabolized' and the virtuoso comparison feel forced.

fact_reason: 'They took money for a pension,' he said. 'I'm sixteen.' (CPP listed on his pay stub and explained by his mother). Employers do not deduct CPP contributions from employees under 18 (canada.ca / CRA). Also lists 'the transit pass' as a claimable item; the federal public transit credit ended in 2017.
age_reason: Tax mechanics are carried by a mother-son story; whose tuition credit it is gets confusing.

fact_reason: 'She checked the arithmetic twice, dividing 585 by 58.44, and got 10.006.' 585 / 58.44 = 10.010, not 10.006.
'The graph was the Mauna Loa carbon dioxide record, a century squashed into one axis.' The Mauna Loa record began in March 1958, so it covers under 70 years, not a century (Wikipedia, Keeling Curve).

'using her dorm address and her mother's maiden name for the last four digits of her social.' Voter registration forms ask for the last four digits of the Social Security number, which are numbers; a mother's maiden name cannot stand in for them.
age_reason: Fits grade 12; one confusing detail ('mother's maiden name for the last four digits of her social').

fact_reason: 'On the food bills there was nothing like it, because the tax was already inside the menu prices.' In Canada restaurant menu prices exclude GST/HST, which is added and listed separately on the customer's bill (pvtistes.net Canadian sales tax guide; Daily Hive).

'He said the tradition calls the broader obligation a fence, a fence around the law.' A 'fence around the Torah' (Pirkei Avot 1:1) means extra rabbinic safeguards against breaking a law. It is not the name for extending the parapet duty to other hazards (Wikipedia, 'Fence around the Torah').

age_reason: Story loses track of its own facts: the 18-year-old won a contest 'Three years earlier, in fifth grade' 'even at ten', and the Alvarez scene ('turned out the way Mr. Alvarez always did') is garbled and goes nowhere.

fact_reason: The story says 36 g of hydrogen reacting with oxygen gives 'Eighteen grams' of water. 36 g H2 is 18 mol, which gives 18 mol H2O, or 324 g of water. The mole method the story teaches gives 324 g, not 18 g.
age_reason: Plot loses track of its own numbers ('Twelve hundred,' then 'so I said 36 grams of water', with 36 g of hydrogen giving '18'), which makes the central insight confusing.

fact_reason: 'Her laptop was open to the UCAS page... The deadline was midnight.' The UCAS January equal-consideration deadline is 18:00 UK time, not midnight (UCAS key-dates pages).
age_reason: Fits grade 12 in voice and pressure; open ending allowed.

fact_reason: 'This is most of it. This one can.' The can holds 890 mg x 2.5 servings = 2,225 mg (about 2.2 g) of sodium, which is more than the whole 2 g WHO daily limit, not 'most of it'.

'Six point two percent of one hundred seventy-one is ten point six zero two... The number was the number.' The story treats Social Security as the only paycheck deduction, but employers must also withhold 1.45% Medicare tax on all wages (IRS Topic 751). Also, a hardware-store cashier hitting the Social Security wage limit (about $184,500 in 2026) by August is not realistic.
age_reason: Fits grade 12; Social Security explanation is brief and dramatized.

fact_reason: 'It's been five percent since January 1, 2008. Before that, from when it started on January 1, 1991, it was seven percent.' The GST was cut to 6% on July 1, 2006, and then to 5% on January 1, 2008 (Wikipedia, Goods and services tax (Canada)). The injected fact's two dates are right.

'The reaction was a one-to-one affair, he was fairly sure, hydrate to anhydrous salt' and the 6.4 g theoretical yield of blue crystals. Blue crystals grown by evaporating aqueous copper sulfate are the pentahydrate (anhydrous CuSO4 is white), so the theoretical yield is about 10.0 g and the percent yield about 41%, not 64%.

'pushed the sliding weight up a few more notches, faster than she had ever set it.' On a mechanical metronome, moving the weight up the pendulum makes the tempo slower, not faster (source: Wikipedia, Metronome).
age_reason: Sophisticated reflection on achievement and learning; required words fit naturally.

fact_reason: '...how are you, obāchan' is said to her grandfather. Obāchan (おばあちゃん) means grandmother; grandfather is ojīchan (japanesewithanime.com).
age_reason: Grief and inherited ritual handled with restraint and fitting complexity.

fact_reason: 'adding up her rectangles again, all thirty of them, and getting 8.8275.' For y = x^2 on [0,3] with 30 rectangles the left sum is 8.555, the right sum 9.455 and the midpoint sum 8.9975; none gives 8.8275.
age_reason: Unreliable narration and shifting viewpoint fit grade 12.
Several hard words used wrongly: 'an expression of pure, alluvial despair', 'the committee would enfranchise whoever spent the most money'.

fact_reason: 'chose a greenish paper for the hill so the gray above it would cool toward something like evening.' Under simultaneous contrast, the law the story itself states, a gray next to green shifts toward green's complement (reddish/pinkish, i.e. warmer), not cooler.
age_reason: Strong band fit; 'could not disenfranchise its surroundings' is a forced use of the required word.
Plot contradicts itself: Deja draws on the napkin, but it then bears 'in his father's handwriting ... held up fine'; also strained 'extrinsic' and 'dichotomize them less'.

fact_reason: 'the aluminum frame that had been bent so many times by deliveries that it had gone ductile, soft at the corner'. Repeated bending work-hardens and fatigues aluminum, making it less ductile, not more.
age_reason: Good inner reasoning about wanting to be wronged; the door frame that has 'gone ductile' is a misused word.
Plot contradicts itself and forces a required word: 'But Vanessa lived in Ohio' vs the manager's 'Here in Ohio?', and the muddled 'You know what a gourmand is?' aside.

The plot loses track of its characters: Priya speaks of herself in the third person ('Mrs. Trujillo circled mine the first time and Priya fixed it after,' Priya said), and the math teacher is 'he', then Mrs. Trujillo, then the debate coach.

fact_reason: 'they could pay the first month plus the deposit at signing, twelve hundred.' With $900 rent and a one-month deposit, first month plus deposit is $1,800, not $1,200.
age_reason: Grade 12 level overall, but expository passages on rent and mortgages, a muddled deposit sum ('twelve hundred'), and a misused 'trenchant' weaken it.
Thinking sits well below grade 12: a concrete 'mise en place' planning lesson ('You'll know for next time') with no competing values or abstraction.

fact_reason: 'thirty-five and thirty-four sitting side by side... the one vote... between them.' The Senate voted 35 to convict when 36 were needed (35-19); 34 has no role, and the one-vote gap is between 35 and 36 (Wikipedia, Impeachment trial of Andrew Johnson).
'Isabelle marries Heathcliff to escape her brother's control'. The character in Wuthering Heights is Isabella Linton, not Isabelle.
age_reason: Rival critical lenses fit grade 12, but the lens is explained lecture-style at the start and 'Bront�' is garbled.

fact_reason: 'One driveway, one evening, forty free throws total.' Everybody shot twenty and at least three players (Dez, Marcus, JJ) are counted, so the total is at least sixty, not forty.
age_reason: Hot-hand study tested and qualified with nuanced uncertainty; fits grade 12 well.

fact_reason: 'She tested it ... dabbing a smear on the inside of her wrist, and it set in under a minute, dry to the touch.' The wrist or lip dab checks the chocolate's temperature. Chocolate does not set on skin at about body temperature; the setting test uses parchment or a knife at room temperature and takes about 3-5 minutes (tastingtable.com; culinaryartsswitzerland.com).

'let the smear sit thirty seconds. It set dull and streaked' / 'the smear set in fifteen seconds with a shine'. A tempered test smear takes roughly 2-5 minutes to set at room temperature, and untempered chocolate does not set (or show bloom) within 30 seconds (King Arthur Baking tempering guide). Also 'It bends instead' overstates compound chocolate's weaker snap.

The story says the two answers differed 'not by a sign flip but by some stranger wrongness' and then blames Priya integrating lower minus upper. Reversing the order only negates the integral, so that mistake gives exactly a sign flip.
age_reason: Math reasoning shown in the scene; 'riparian and biome' poster is a contrived way in for the required words.

fact_reason: The story has the K. 332 Adagio wander through keys in a development before the recapitulation. That movement is in sonatina form with no development section (Wikipedia, 'Piano Sonata No. 12 (Mozart)'); after the double bar the theme returns at once, turning to B-flat minor.
age_reason: Hearing sonata form at a live concert, with a mistaken placement corrected; the tone fits the age.

fact_reason: 'The children at the top of the chart, the narrow head, were the school question; the near-empty peak was the nursing home question.' In a population pyramid the youngest age groups are the bottom bars and the oldest are at the top, so children cannot be at the top.
age_reason: Playful and open-ended at the right level; minor slip placing the 'narrow head of children' at the top of the chart.

fact_reason: 'His father had voted the night before at the advance poll.' Canadian federal advance polls run on the 10th to 7th days before polling day, not the night before (Canada Elections Act s.171(2), laws-lois.justice.gc.ca).

age_reason: Idea sits well below grade 12: the whole insight is 'The red arrows. Warm water. The blue ones are cold.', with no competing values or abstraction.

fact_reason: 'She was sixteen, three years too young to vote.' That implies a voting age of 19, which no country uses; the voting age in the UK and Canada (the setting's spelling and polling terms) is 18 (Wikipedia, Voting age).
'two hours a day, five years, or one hour a day for ten' as a route to ten thousand hours: both come to about 3,650 hours, not 10,000 (2 h/day would take about 13.7 years).

'Eight percent, plus the provincial part.' Ontario HST is 13%: 5% federal plus 8% provincial (CRA/Ontario.ca). Also: a 16-year-old's stub shows CPP, but CPP is not deducted for employees under 18 (CRA payroll rules); and 'The bus passes qualified' is wrong, since employee commuting costs are not deductible in Canada (CRA general rule).
age_reason: Tax concepts shown through a wry, well-paced scene with apt grade-12 vocabulary.

fact_reason: The stub shows $352 gross and $330 net with Social Security ($21.82) plus one small other line. US employers must also withhold Medicare at 1.45% (about $5.10 here), so net pay could not be $330 (IRS Topic 751). Also flagged: a 17-year-old being taught the restaurant slicer. Minors under 18 may not operate power-driven meat slicers under FLSA Hazardous Occupations Order 10 (29 CFR 570.61), but the story does not say the slicer is powered.

'Rambam says cruelty.' In Guide for the Perplexed III:48 Maimonides explains the meat-and-milk ban as gross, over-filling food probably linked to idolatrous festival practice, not cruelty; the cruelty/compassion reading comes from other commentators (Guide III:48, via Sefaria source sheet).
age_reason: Strong competing-values debate; a confusing 'not about his own brother' line muddles family relations.

fact_reason: 'the official answer: twelve meters... launch speed twelve point four', and then 'Air' explains the ball landing farther than the recalculation. At 12.4 m/s and 30 degrees the vacuum range is about 13.6 m, not 12 m, and air resistance shortens a flight; it cannot make a ball go farther than the prediction.
age_reason: Fits grade 12, but the hint-button twist ('official answer ... twelve meters') is confusing, and 'You do the logos' is forced.

fact_reason: 'the warm-up would take the first ten minutes... It's called the FIFA 11 plus' and 'Nine of us here, that's like three fewer seasons ending on a stretcher.' The 11+ used in the 2008 Norwegian trial is a roughly 20-minute programme (Soligard et al., BMJ 2008), and a one-third cut in injury rate does not mean three of nine players spared.
'the F on the top space of the treble staff where it belonged.' The top space of the treble staff is E; F (F5) sits on the top line.

age_reason: Info-dump via the cousin's text on Tuckman's stages, and a garbled ending in which the absent coach says 'I was the one doing the storming theory.'

fact_reason: '...the scene where Nelly watches Catherine through a keyhole and Heathcliff watches through the same keyhole...' There is no keyhole scene: Catherine confides in Nelly in the kitchen and Heathcliff, unseen, overhears only up to 'it would degrade me to marry Heathcliff' (CliffsNotes/SparkNotes ch. 9). The 'warned Heathcliff about Hindley's plan to separate him from Catherine' episode is also not in the novel.
age_reason: Fits; 'something with sentience of its own' misuses the word and there is an 'overCards' typo.

fact_reason: 'So the money I put in now is worth ten times more than money I put in later. Like, at forty.' At 7% a year, money invested at 18 rather than at 40 grows by an extra factor of 1.07^22, which is about 4.4, not ten. The story's own figure of $14,974 is correct.
age_reason: Compounding set against wisdom or cage, left unresolved; fits grade 12.

fact_reason: 'She had checked the key signature on the score, and there it was, one sharp where there had been none.' In a Mozart C major sonata exposition the key signature does not change. The move to G major is written with accidentals (F sharps), not a new key signature.
age_reason: Sonata-form analysis is shown through a lesson and an argued uncertainty; the 'logos' exchange at the end is forced.

fact_reason: '...watched the thermometer climb through the rest... arriving almost exactly where her grandmother's card had said the meat should finish [160]... the center came up rosy and correct.' A roast at 160°F is well done, not rosy; well done is about 155°F and up, medium-rare about 130-135°F (ThermoWorks beef temperature guide). Carryover cooking is described correctly.

'editors pushing back on the owner over a planned endorsement, and the paper's editorial board overriding it.' In 2024 Soon-Shiong blocked the board's planned Harris endorsement and it did not run; editorials editor Mariel Garza resigned (cjr.org, axios.com).
age_reason: Fits grade 12 with competing views of media ownership and existentialism applied; 'alluvial light' is forced.
Corrupted foreign-script text breaks a sentence: 'pulling the失败的 batch toward the edge of the table'.

fact_reason: The story places the end of K. 333's second movement development at measure 98 and a retransition around measure 90, with a false recapitulation in the wrong key. That movement is 82 measures long: development mm. 32-50, recapitulation from m. 51 (PTNA piano encyclopedia, enc.piano.or.jp).
age_reason: Playful discovery of a retransition with an open question about enjoying being fooled.

fact_reason: 'She drew a small dot after the half note, then counted: the note, and the dot, one-two-three, and the fourth beat of silence before the next bar began, and the bar was full.' The rhythm maths doesn't add up. The bar was one beat short, so the dot's extra beat should fill it with no leftover silence. And a 4/4 bar holding a three-beat dotted half is only full if a quarter note or quarter rest is written, not an unwritten 'beat of silence'. The injected fact itself is stated correctly.
age_reason: Competing values of reverence and ambition, left unresolved, fit grade 12, but the beat-count logic is muddled ('a beat missing' vs 'She needed three').

fact_reason: '128 over 76... The first reading was fine, under both thresholds.' Under the same 2017 ACC/AHA guideline, 120-129 over less than 80 is 'elevated', not normal (Wikipedia, Blood pressure).

The story places the end of the first theme and the start of the busy transition at m. 22 of K. 333, but the transition runs mm. 11-22 and the second theme begins at m. 23 in F major. It also says K. 309's second theme comes back 'in the same key as the first, no new key at all', but in K. 309 the second theme is in G major, the dominant (Unisa K. 309 analysis; K. 333 analyses).
age_reason: Strong fit; 'an ascetic discipline of appearances' is a strained use.

fact_reason: 'It was always ten yards ahead of wherever the ball was' (also 'on third down... ten yards past the ball'). The line to gain is set 10 yards from the start of a series and stays fixed until a first down or change of possession, so on later downs it is usually less than 10 yards away (source: NCAA Rule 5, line to gain).
age_reason: Well-written, but the reasoning (how the yellow line is drawn) sits a little light for grade 12.

fact_reason: 'Nicholas took the petitioner's table' to argue the student's side, then argued the school's side 'at the respondent's table'. In Mahanoy Area School District v. B.L. the school district was the petitioner and B.L. was the respondent (Wikipedia). Minor: B.L. was suspended from the cheerleading squad, not 'suspended' from school.
age_reason: Well-pitched mock-court story, dinged by forced or odd words ('crepuscular in the late morning', 'the nod coagulated', a biome simile) and Nicholas being called 'Ms. Reyes'.

fact_reason: 'a deposit of five weeks, which meant five sevenths of a month's rent, which meant roughly £518.' A month is about 4.35 weeks, not 7; five weeks of £725/month rent is 725x12/52x5, about £837.
age_reason: Fits, but the rent figures (GBP 725 vs 900) are confusing.

fact_reason: 'thirty years after publishing those volumes, Thiers had signed off on shooting Parisians in the streets.' The History appeared 1823-1827 and Thiers crushed the Commune in 1871, about 44 years later (the rue Transnonain killings were 1834); source: Wikipedia, Adolphe Thiers.
'The novel was "The Tell-Tale Heart," all fourteen pages of it.' 'The Tell-Tale Heart' is a short story, not a novel, and it runs only a few pages.
age_reason: Fits the band; the story is miscalled a 'novel', and 'recidivism' is forced into the family analogy.

fact_reason: Aron's questions are misnumbered and misquoted: 'When did you last sing to yourself?' is question 5, not the first (Q1 is the dinner-guest question), question 20 is 'What does friendship mean to you?', and the regret question is Q33 (source: Psychology Today list of Aron's 36 questions). Injected fact itself is stated correctly.

The empty bag reads 'Twenty-six grams', then Emma adds magnesium ribbon and powder and 'The needle didn't move. Twenty-six grams, sealed.' Adding material to the bag must increase its mass; conservation of mass means mass is unchanged by the reaction, not by adding reactants.

age_reason: Garbled statistics dialogue confuses the scene: 'Sixteen people out of a hundred' / 'Four point a half,' and 'one and a half someones harder'.

fact_reason: 'You did the complement backwards. You just wrote the same letters in reverse order' CTAATGT is the correct base-pair complement of GATTACA, not its reverse, so only the T's needed to become U's (CUAAUGU). Also, 'The fourth one. In DNA it's an A' is wrong: the fourth base of GATTACA is T.
age_reason: Central scene contradicts itself: 'You did the complement backwards', yet the rewrite produces the same strand, 'CTAATGT again', which muddles the lesson.

fact_reason: 'The Second Sex, Simone de Beauvoir, the translation dated 1949 on the copyright page.' The book was published in French in 1949; the first English translation (Parshley) came out in 1953 (MIT Libraries 150 Books). The quotation and the 1949 original publication are otherwise correct.
age_reason: Strong competing-lens reasoning; slight grammar slip in 'something that malign men as a class'.

fact_reason: 'The white dress is this kind of impermeable surface, nothing gets in, blood goes everywhere else but the dress stays white.' In The Two Fridas blood from the vessel cut by the forceps spills onto the European Frida's white dress (Wikipedia, The Two Fridas); she also holds forceps, not scissors.
age_reason: Formal analysis of Kahlo with competing interpretations and self-questioning fits grade 12 well.

fact_reason: 'The feminist sheet said Charlotte Bronte had to publish under a man's name' about Wuthering Heights. Wuthering Heights is by Emily Bronte, published as Ellis Bell (Wikipedia, Wuthering Heights).

The story has (low + high) / 2 overflow on a 200-million-element array. With 32-bit ints, low + high stays under about 400 million, far below 2,147,483,647; overflow needs arrays of more than about 1.07 billion elements.

'And I don't have EI either. I have QPIP.' Quebec employees still pay EI premiums, at a reduced rate (1.31% in 2025), with QPIP replacing only the parental benefits (canada.ca EI premium report). Also: Noor from Quebec says her stub reads CPP and Ava's reads QPP (reversed), and 17-year-old Ava's stub shows CPP, which is not deducted for employees under 18 (CRA payroll rules).
age_reason: Fits grade 12; one expository paragraph on Quebec vs. Canada deductions reads like a textbook aside.

fact_reason: 'They got to the maror later, after the Hillel sandwich.' In the seder, maror is eaten on its own first and korech (the Hillel sandwich) comes right after it (myjewishlearning.com, 14 steps of the seder). Also, horseradish is the answer given to 'what is that green stuff', but horseradish is not green.

'Forty-five degrees down to eighty-one, seed, hold' and dipping at 'eighty-two. Close enough to hold.' This mixes Celsius and Fahrenheit, and 81-82 F (27-28 C) is the cooling point; tempered dark chocolate is rewarmed to and worked at about 31-32 C (88-90 F) (popsci.com / foodnetwork.com tempering guides).
age_reason: Good fit; sugar-bloom explanation leans toward exposition.

fact_reason: 'Eight hundred against five weeks of five hundred and forty came in just under. Flat B was legal.' At 540 pounds a month, five weeks' rent is about 623 pounds (540 x 12 / 52 x 5), so an 800-pound deposit is over the cap and Flat B's deposit is not legal either.
age_reason: Good fit; forced opening simile ('the steppe of her imagination') and an odd 'recently been eighteen' for a middle-aged man.

fact_reason: 'a pyramid, wide at the base, narrowing to a thread at the top, with the label Japan beneath it... more like a barrel... for Niger.' This is reversed: Niger, with very high fertility, has the wide-based pyramid, and Japan's is barrel-shaped or top-heavy.
age_reason: Good reasoning for the band, but the pyramid description is muddled ('filling in at the bottom' while the base thins).

fact_reason: The story has Annabelle eat rice and chicken that 'sat at the back of the fridge... for five days' after reheating it to 165 F, as if reheating solves the question of age. USDA says to keep leftovers in the fridge for only 3-4 days (usda.gov leftovers guidance), and reheating does not make older leftovers safe.

'It wanted allowances and withholdings...' The Form W-4 has not used withholding allowances since the 2020 redesign; it now asks for dollar amounts for dependents, other income and deductions (IRS newsroom on the 2020 W-4).

The endorsed data show 30 degrees giving about 16 ft, 60 degrees 8 ft and 45 degrees 31 ft. At a fixed launch speed, range goes as sin 2θ, so 30 and 60 degrees should each give about 87% of the 45-degree range. The story also says 45 degrees is the maximum 'with actual still air', but air resistance pushes the best angle below 45 degrees.
age_reason: Good hands-on inquiry, but the thinking is mostly mechanism-level for grade 12, and 'putative lawn mower' is a strained word use.

fact_reason: 'You're supposed to charge HST.' A private individual selling a used personal item generally does not charge GST/HST (CRA personal-use property rules), and the store charges GST plus a separate 7% provincial tax, so it is not in an HST province anyway. Also: 17-year-old Jasmine's stub shows CPP, but CPP is not deducted for employees under 18 (CRA payroll rules).
age_reason: Tax systems compared through a scene; 'felt almost like arbitrage' is acknowledged as imprecise.

fact_reason: On the fourth night 'the flames doubled themselves ... so that nine became eighteen, the eight and the helper both.' On the fourth night only five lights burn (four candles plus the shamash). Also, 'Right to left, and you take them out left to right' garbles the rule, which is to add candles right to left and light them left to right (Chabad.org).

'the maid who packed Jane's trunk in the middle of the crisis, working while Jane wept' (and the mother's 'The maid packing while Jane stands there'). In Jane Eyre, Jane's trunks were already packed and corded before the wedding (ch. 25). She leaves them behind and flees with only a small parcel (ch. 27; Rochester later says 'your trunks were left corded and locked'). Source: Project Gutenberg text #1260.

'He reversed the two arguments in his assertEquals, ran the test, and watched the bar turn green.' Swapping expected and actual only changes the failure message. assertEquals(14.99, 24.99) fails either way, so the swap cannot make a failing test pass (the girl's test 'Green.' has the same error).
age_reason: Suspenseful story about the order of assertEquals arguments with fitting reflection; the required words are placed somewhat decoratively.

fact_reason: The story sets the watch party at the July 2018 World Cup final and has a tied score, an 87th-minute VAR-reviewed penalty and a 90th-minute winner. France beat Croatia 4-2; the VAR penalty was awarded for a Perisic handball and scored by Griezmann in the 38th minute (SI.com, The Week match reports).
age_reason: Mature inner conflict fits, but the plot slips: 'the commentators lionize' and 'still losing' after a tied score.

fact_reason: 'a small silver thing with a fat yellow L stuck to its back' - UK L plates must be a red L on a white background (source: GOV.UK, using L and P plates). Injected fact is stated correctly.

The worked example is impossible: a cubic with f(0)=2, f(6)=11 and a critical point at 3.5 with value 4 has f''(3.5)>0, so the 'second derivative' could not show 'a peak and not a valley.' No cubic has a local maximum of 4 at x=3.5 with those endpoint values (recomputed).

age_reason: Text glitches would trip a reader ('the十六 different kinds of sandpaper', 'malign ed the whole unit'), and her age contradicts itself (November vs December, 'you're sixteen').

fact_reason: 'a single blood vessel connected them, winding down out of one heart, looped through their joined hands, and back up into the other.' In The Two Fridas the vessel runs directly between the two hearts; the clasped hands are a separate link, and the vessel's ends go to the Diego miniature in the right Frida's hand and the surgical clamp in the left Frida's lap (Wikipedia/Sartle/Britannica descriptions). Also the Tehuana dress is not 'reds and golds' (its skirt is olive green).
age_reason: Interpretive ambiguity fits grade 12; 'obstreperous energy' for clearing a table is a loose fit.

fact_reason: 'It's not ritual. It's not about the temple. It's sandwiched between laws about theft and lying.' Leviticus 19:9-10 is preceded by 19:5-8 on sacrifices of well-being (ritual law) and followed by 19:11 on stealing and lying (BibleGateway, NRSVUE).
age_reason: Textual argument over Leviticus with competing readings and an unresolved question fits grade 12 well.

fact_reason: '...the desert horizon, the coral band of the dress.' In The Broken Column, Kahlo wears no dress. She is nude except for a white corset and a sheet wrapped around her lower body (Wikipedia, The Broken Column). The injected fact about the nails, tears and direct gaze is stated correctly.
age_reason: Mature first-person reflection on art and grief; excellent grade 12 fit.

fact_reason: uncertain: story calls the A string the 'second string' and B the 'fifth string' (counting up from low E as a tuning sequence); standard guitar numbering is 5th = A, 2nd = B.

'I had cast Dev as Filer, the complainer' in Pinter's 'Trouble in the Works'. The sketch's two characters are Mr Fibbs (the boss) and Wills (the works man reporting the complaints); there is no Filer (Wikipedia, Trouble in the Works).
age_reason: Plot loses its own timeline: he is already at the rehearsal, then 'I got back to the annex at two, exactly as I'd promised Priya I would, only two hours later than she'd expected me.'

fact_reason: 'a lopsided triangle, sliced it into floors, and labeled them from bottom to top: exposition, rising action, climax, falling action, resolution' (resolution then called 'that last narrow floor'). In Freytag's pyramid the climax is the apex, and falling action and resolution come down the other side; source: Wikipedia, Dramatic structure.

'Against the orange the gray bent warm. Against the green it bent cool.' (and 'warm over the sunset, cool over the pines'). Under Chevreul's law the gray shifts toward the neighbor's complement: next to orange it looks bluish/cool, next to green reddish/warm (Wikipedia, Michel Eugène Chevreul). The fact sentence itself is quoted correctly but its demonstration is reversed.

'two moles of water for every mole of oxygen'. In CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O there is one mole of water per mole of O2 (5.0 g O2 = 0.156 mol gives 0.156 mol H2O). Also 'how many sandwiches... Two... Right.': two slices of bread make one sandwich, so the limiting-reactant analogy is miscounted.
age_reason: Reads young for grade 12: a peer tutors a sandwich analogy ('Whatever runs out first is what caps the product') with a neat resolution and no competing values.

fact_reason: 'the two gases inside had settled into their balanced state, half one compound and half the other.' Equilibrium means the forward and reverse rates are equal, not that the amounts are equal; the NO2/N2O4 mixture is not half and half.
age_reason: Right level, but the opening note is taped by Sadie and signed Marcus, and 'sensitized' is forced in twice in a row.

fact_reason: 'patted it dry with paper towels instead, which the page also mentioned.' The CDC raw-chicken page (cdc.gov/food-safety/foods/chicken.html) says not to wash chicken but does not mention patting it dry. The injected fact is stated correctly.

'The answer unfolded along the cold blue to warm pink line the demo had shown.' In the cobalt chloride equilibrium the solution is pink when cold and blue when hot (NCSSM and Temple chem-demo notes). The equation is also misnamed: 'CoCl6' is not a species in it; it is [Co(H2O)6]2+ against [CoCl4]2-.
age_reason: Misused word ('her mother disenfranchising the whole idea of pre-calculus') is a small minus.

fact_reason: 'The exposition she could feel closing around bar ninety-three' and the development fragment 'in the middle of the storm, bar one hundred and six'. In K. 333/I the exposition ends at bar 63, the development runs about bars 64-93 and the recapitulation begins at bar 93/94, so bar 106 is in the recapitulation (Pearson Edexcel A-level K. 333 analysis, found via search).

'the laundromat unit, nine hundred and ninety if heat and water together came in under a hundred and forty' The laundromat rent is $890 ($60 less than $950), so a $990 total means $100 of utilities, not 'under $140'; the story's worked total does not add up (and leaves out hydro, which that lease also excludes).
age_reason: Grade-12 prose, but the lease-law explanation leans expository and 'peccadillo' is forced.

fact_reason: 'She had written void in front of it... the compiler had never complained' while the tester printed 0.0, then deleting void gave 250.0. With only a void method Account(String,double), Java supplies just a no-arg constructor, so a tester passing the owner and 250 would not compile; one calling new Account() would stop compiling once the real constructor is added. The shown before/after sequence is impossible Java.

'He says he's tapping Ackley on the shoulder to say goodnight, and then he admits the whole thing was a lie.' No such scene is in the novel; Holden's Ackley scenes (ch. 3, 7) contain no confessed goodnight lie (LitCharts ch. 3 and ch. 7 summaries). The 'terrific liar' line leads into his lie to Mr. Spencer about the gym; the quote and 1951 date are correct.
age_reason: Unreliable-narrator analysis carried through dialogue suits grade 12, with small slips like 'deliberate on purpose' and the odd closing line 'Ask me again in 1951.'

fact_reason: 'Nick claims to reserve judgment in the third chapter.' Nick says he is 'inclined to reserve all judgments' on the opening page of Chapter 1; the 'honest people' line closes Chapter 3 (History Hit Chapter 1 text).
age_reason: Right level; odd images such as 'the reflection of the sound sat under the water' and 'mattress bar suturing'.

fact_reason: uncertain: teacher's claim 'Groucho Marx had one [a guitar tuning of his own]'. Groucho did play guitar (Gibson L-5, Horse Feathers), but no source found for a tuning of his.

fact_reason: The story misnumbers Aron's 36 questions: 'change one thing about the way I was raised' is question 10, not nine (9 is 'most grateful'); 'When did you last cry in front of another person' is 30, not in the twenties; 28 is not about dying; 'whose death would you find most disturbing' is 35, not 36 (36 is sharing a personal problem). Source: published Aron list at amorebeautifulquestion.com/36-questions.

'...tied to the red of the ribbon in her hair, the small red of the bird.' The hummingbird in Kahlo's Self-Portrait with Thorn Necklace and Hummingbird is black, not red (Wikipedia article on the painting).
'the American arrangement: a president elected directly' The US president is chosen indirectly, by the Electoral College (Article II and the 12th Amendment), not by direct popular vote.
age_reason: Strong ideas, but 'delimitated' is a wrong word form.
Contradicts its own lesson that only nouns are capitalized: 'bellicose, which Levi at first misread as a place name because it was capitalized... it could not be a noun if it mattered where it sat'.

fact_reason: 'We didn't even go that far... Crossed the county line, that's it. Rhinebeck to Red Hook.' Rhinebeck and Red Hook are neighbouring towns both in Dutchess County, NY (Wikipedia), so there is no county line and no sales-tax difference between them. Also, the mother's note 'If you don't file you lose the money they took out' is left uncorrected; a US taxpayer owed a refund generally has three years to claim it.
age_reason: Paycheque and sales-tax reasoning is worked through by Evan himself; fits the band.

fact_reason: 'Carlyle wrote as if... a "dread chasseur" hunting France toward doom.' The quoted phrase does not appear in Carlyle's The French Revolution (Project Gutenberg full text checked); it is a quotation invented and attributed to him.
age_reason: Fits grade 12; the dinner-argument dialogue attribution is briefly muddled.

fact_reason: 'If you're not back by four, I have to send you home. I can't put you on the clock without it' (his passport). Only Section 1 is due by the first day; the employee may present identity documents within 3 business days of the first day of paid work (source: USCIS M-274 Handbook, section 4.0). Injected fact is stated correctly.

'Fourteen names had NULL beside them, and at the top... was Mr. Halloran.' Halloran has an order (the 1998 plum tree), so a Customers LEFT JOIN Orders returns that order row for him, not NULL; NULL only appears for customers with no orders at all.
age_reason: Arguing both ways over a query result fits grade 12; 'beseeching the grandfather's router' is slightly awkward.

fact_reason: 'Ellis, took three straight fastballs for strikes... Ellis bunted.' In baseball three strikes is a strikeout, so the batter cannot stay at the plate and bunt afterwards (judged on knowledge of the rules).

'Kennan wires Moscow, says the Soviets are expansionist.' Kennan sent the Long Telegram from the US embassy in Moscow to the State Department in Washington (Feb. 22, 1946; CFR/teachingamericanhistory.org).

The learner practises merging onto a motorway at seventy miles an hour with her grandmother before passing her test, and the story treats this as fine. Under Highway Code rule 253 (gov.uk), a learner on a GB motorway must be with an approved driving instructor in a dual-control car.
'in a fifty-year-old paper's small collapse' refers to the Los Angeles Times, which was first published in 1881 and was about 143 years old in 2024 (source: Wikipedia, Los Angeles Times).

fact_reason: 'Nineteen feet four inches.' ... 'That's half a foot of margin of error.' A 22-foot prediction against a 19 ft 4 in landing is a 2 ft 8 in gap, not half a foot; the error is never corrected.
age_reason: Fits grade 12, but 'half a foot of margin of error' contradicts the shots landing about 2.5 feet short.

fact_reason: 'it's hilarious because he doesn't clock that they're con men for the longest time.' In Chapter 19 Huck says 'It didn't take me long to make up my mind that these liars warn't no kings nor dukes at all, but just low-down humbugs and frauds'; he sees through them almost at once and keeps quiet (text checked via search of Ch. 19, storgy.com/Goodreads quotations).

'She counted the key signature on the page. E-flat major.' A C minor movement already carries a three-flat key signature, the same as E-flat major, so counting the key signature cannot show the second theme is in E-flat; the key is identified from the harmony and accidentals.

age_reason: Timeline contradicts itself: 'the workshop was tomorrow at nine' vs 'two days before he had to explain consent' vs 'Friday morning', and a high-schooler 'rehearsing, in his dorm room'.

fact_reason: 'Minus 18 degrees Celsius on average, the narrator said' about the Moon, and 'the Earth did, at minus 18, before the blanket.' The Moon's mean temperature is far colder (about -60 C at the equator per Diviner, UCLA), and -18 C is a hypothetical Earth with no greenhouse effect, not an actual past state of Earth. The injected -18/14 fact itself is stated correctly.
age_reason: Core insight is middle-school level ('So greenhouse gases are a blanket, not a villain') with jokey banter, and 'That's the chicanery' misuses the required word.

fact_reason: 'He did the arithmetic again, this time without the tax, and the number came out under his savings by almost forty dollars.' The $899 laptop is $259 more than his $640 savings, even with no tax. The follow-up claim is also wrong: adding the roughly $90 from the missed shift gives $730, which still does not cover the laptop 'tax or no tax'.
age_reason: The story's own numbers contradict: $899 laptop against $640 saved, yet without tax it 'came out under his savings by almost forty dollars'.

fact_reason: Pay stub shows $99.00 gross reduced to $62.41 net by federal tax, state tax and FICA. FICA is 7.65% (about $7.57), and federal withholding on a $99 paycheck is $0 under IRS Pub 15-T standard withholding, so net pay would be near $88-91, not $62 (judged on knowledge; search confirmed only older Pub 15-T tables also give $0). Injected sales-tax fact is stated correctly.

age_reason: Plot loses track: an evening festival text is read 'during second period study hall', and Arianna wonders 'whether she'd tell Jess about the recording' when Jess told her about it.

fact_reason: 'The second it touches the horizon, we eat.' Iftar begins when the sun has completely set (the whole disc below the horizon, i.e. maghrib), not when it first touches the horizon (IslamQA/Hanafi fatwa on sunset timing).
age_reason: Reflective and age-appropriate; the plot blurs whether the iftar happens at the cemetery or at home.

fact_reason: 'That's not even.' / 'That's the point.' The story presents an odd amount ($35) as the right red-envelope gift. Tradition favours even amounts, and odd amounts are associated with funerals (Wikipedia, Red envelope). The rule about avoiding four is stated correctly.
age_reason: Belief that is false but load-bearing, shown subtly through family scene; excellent fit.

fact_reason: 'The sky was torn open by fissures the same pale grey as the column.' In The Broken Column the fissures are in the arid, cracked ground; the sky is stormy, not fissured (Wikipedia, The Broken Column).
